title: Network guardrail prototype PRD (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc sketches an MVP for customer-managed network guardrails that combine structured audit logs, policy-driven approval gates, and a compact evidence bundle suitable for forensic replay. This is intentionally scoped small: early customers should be able to opt into an approval + evidence workflow for VPC changes that integrates with our private deployment control plane.

Why now / background:
- Several pilot customers asked for an auditable way to accept, review, and rollback network config changes in Private deployments.
- We currently export raw syslogs and packet-level telemetry; customers need a higher-level, signed trail that ties operator intent -> approval -> applied change.
- Security/compliance requests are blocking a handful of deals; a lightweight guardrail feature could unlock those.

Goals (MVP):
- Provide a compact, signed audit event for each operator-initiated network change that includes pre/post state diffs and a human-readable rationale.
- Add a policy-driven approval gate that can: require 0/1/n approvers, enforce time-based hold windows, and attach evidence tokens to approvals.
- Offer an API and UI endpoint to fetch an "evidence bundle" for a change: audit events, operator id, approval artifacts, and relevant telemetry links.
- Make audit log schema usable by customers’ SIEMs (JSON-lines, stable field names, simple timestamping).

Non-goals (MVP exclusions):
- Full-blown attestation framework with HSM-signed receipts (we may mock signatures using platform signing keys initially).
- Deep packet capture or long-term telemetry retention beyond 90 days.
- Auto-rollback orchestration (manual rollback steps only for MVP).

Success metrics (90 days post-launch):
- 3 pilot customers onboarded to guardrails workflow.
- 90% of listed change events include a linked evidence bundle (searchable from Console).
- Customer CSAT >= 4.0 on audit/evidence UX for pilot participants.

User stories:
- As a customer network operator, I want to submit a VPC-change and request approver sign-off so I can make high-risk changes during business hours with oversight.
- As a security reviewer, I want to see a compact evidence bundle that proves who approved a change and why, plus the pre/post network ACLs, so I can satisfy internal auditors.
- As a SRE on Redwood, I want to fetch the evidence bundle via API for quick incident triage.

Requirements (high-level):
- Audit event schema with stable fields: event_id, change_type, operator_id, operator_email, timestamp, resource_id, before_snapshot (compact), after_snapshot (compact), diff_summary, reason_text, request_id, approval_refs (list), evidence_bundle_url, platform_signature_meta.
- Approval workflow API: POST /v1/private/vpc-change-requests create a request; PATCH to add approvals; GET to query status. Support approval states: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED, ESCALATED, EXPIRED.
- Console UX: simple request form, approver list with expiration windows, ability to attach files/links to approval, inline timeline view showing audit events and linked telemetry.
- Evidence bundle format: JSON-lines package (gzipped) with: 1) canonical audit events, 2) approval artifacts (approver id, timestamp, optional comment, signature token), 3) pointers to telemetry (log storage keys) and an index file.
- Retention policy: guardrail evidence bundles retained for 90 days by default; customers may request longer retention via Enterprise add-on.

Design notes / data model (draft):
- event_id: uuid v4
- request_id: user-facing short id (NET-REQ-<6 chars>)
- timestamps: RFC3339
- operator_id/email: canonical user id from SSO (customer->operator mapping)
- before_snapshot/after_snapshot: compact JSON (only changed objects + hashed full snapshot reference)
- diff_summary: short human text generated by platform diff engine (max 500 chars)
- approval_refs: list of approval artifacts: {approver_id, approver_email, approver_role, comment, ts, method} — for MVP store inline in audit event as flattened string fields (e.g. approval_1_id, approval_1_ts).
- platform_signature_meta: {signer: 'redwood-control-plane-v1', sig_type: 'hmac-sha256', sig_version: 'v0'} — stored as string for now.

Approval workflow (behavioral draft):
1) Operator creates change request via Console/API. System creates request_id and PENDING state, emits an initial audit event (type=request_created).
2) Approvers are notified (email + Console). Approver can APPROVE/REJECT/ESCALATE (API). Each action emits an audit event and appends to approval_refs.
3) If required approvals satisfied -> transition to APPROVED. Platform emits pre-deploy audit event and produces evidence bundle URL.
4) Customer operator triggers apply change (separate step) and platform emits apply event with before/after snapshots.
5) Evidence bundle assembled and marked FINAL.
6) If approvals expire (configurable TTL), request goes to EXPIRED and remains visible.

Console UX sketches (notes):
- Single page: top shows request summary + state badge. Below: timeline cards (created, approvals, pre-deploy, apply, evidence bundle link). Right column: approver list + quick-approve buttons.
- Lightweight mobile flow: approvers can approve via email link which directs to a secure approval prompt (no full Console login for initial MVP; SSO link optional).
- Search: filter by request_id, resource_id, operator_email, approver, state, date range.

APIs (MVP endpoints):
- POST /v1/private/vpc-change-requests -> creates request + returns request_id
- GET /v1/private/vpc-change-requests/{id} -> request + linked audit events
- POST /v1/private/vpc-change-requests/{id}/actions -> body {action: 'approve'|'reject'|'escalate', comment, approver_id}
- GET /v1/private/evidence-bundles/{bundle_id} -> signed URL (short-lived)

Operational considerations:
- Need a lightweight queue for approval notifications and webhook retries.
- Evidence bundle generation should be async; assemble in background to avoid blocking apply path.
- Rate limiting: guardrail endpoints accept modest event volume; default quota 500 reqs/min per org.
- Observability: add Console dashboard showing pending approvals, avg approval latency, evidence bundle generation success rate.

Security and compliance sketch:
- Authentication: integrate with customer SSO mapping already used in Private control plane.
- Authorization: map approver roles to RBAC (operator, net-approver, security-officer).
- Integrity: platform-side HMAC signatures on bundles for initial proof-of-origin. Plan for HSM-based signing in subsequent work.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we include complete pre-change configs in every event or store a content-addressed blob and reference it? (tradeoff: storage cost vs. simplicity)
- How to represent multi-resource changes (e.g., route table + ACL + subnet resize) within one request? single request with multiple change entries vs multiple linked requests.
- Customer expectation around legal-grade signatures — need PSG input.
- Escalation policy: do we allow automatic escalation after n hours to a secondary approver? (Yes if pilot customer wants it.)
- How to integrate with existing SIEM ingestion pipelines (format/field naming conventions).

Implementation roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- M0 (2 weeks): final design review, API contracts, schema freeze. Create spike for evidence bundle assembly.
- M1 (6 weeks): backend APIs, minimal Console create/view UX, event emission pipeline.
- M2 (4 weeks): approval actions, email webhook for quick-approve flow, evidence bundle generation.
- M3 (4 weeks): retention/enforcement, observability dashboard, onboarding scripts for pilots.
- Pilot (2–4 weeks): onboard 2–3 customers, collect feedback, iterate.

Dependencies:
- Platform signing/key management APIs (ticket ENG-4492).
- Notification/email infrastructure (Marketing/Infra coordination).
- Telemetry indexer team for log pointers (OBS-1101).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Evidence generation delays could block audits. Mitigation: mark bundles as provisional and allow manual retrieval of raw audit events.
- Risk: Approval UX too heavy for operators -> low adoption. Mitigation: aggressive UX iteration during pilot, support quick-approve via email.
- Risk: Storage costs for full snapshots. Mitigation: store diffs + content-addressed blobs and GC older blobs beyond retention window.

Rollout notes / gating criteria for GA:
- Security review complete and PSG sign-off on signature scheme.
- Pilot customers report no major gaps (CSAT threshold) and LGTM from SRE for evidence bundle reliability.
- Automated tests for event emission and bundle integrity in CI.

Appendix: sample audit event (human-readable):
- request_id: NET-REQ-4a7b9c
- event_type: request_created
- operator: a.menon@acme-corp.com
- ts: 2025-11-12T15:04:22Z
- change_summary: "Add egress ACL rule to allow 10.5.0.0/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0 tcp:443"
- before_hash: sha256:...
- after_hash: sha256:...
- diff_summary: "+1 ACL rule (egress) on acl-22; no other resources changed"
- approvals: "approver_1=rafael.ortega@acme-corp.com;ts=2025-11-12T15:27:00Z;decision=APPROVED;comment=ok for release"
Notes to reviewer: this is intentionally terse — designed to be a starting spec for engineering spike. We should prioritize getting a working end-to-end loop for one common change type (ACL updates) before expanding to full route/table/subnet workflows.

Action items:
- Aisha: schedule design review with ENG, SRE, PSG (week of 2025-11-10).
- Rafael: prototype evidence bundle assembler spike (2 weeks).
- Maya: mock Console flows and email quick-approve copy.
- Tom: scope telemetry indexer changes and estimate storage impact.
